title: Effect of mobile money services on the growth of small businesses in Douala V Municipality (2018–2022)
snippet: This study examined how mobile money use affects sales, savings and access to credit among 214 small business owners in Douala V. Results show that regular users…
abstract: This study examined how mobile money services affect the growth of small businesses in Douala V Municipality. A questionnaire was given to 214 owners selected by stratified sampling, and data were analysed with descriptive statistics and regression. Regular users recorded higher monthly sales and savings, but transaction charges reduced use for very small traders. The study recommends lower charges for small amounts and training on merchant accounts.

title: Mobile money and financial inclusion in Central Africa: a review of evidence
snippet: We review 41 studies published between 2010 and 2022 on mobile money and financial inclusion. Most studies report gains in savings and remittances, but few measure…
abstract: This review brings together 41 studies on mobile money and financial inclusion in Central Africa. Most report better access to savings and remittances, especially for rural households. Few studies measure long-term effects on small business growth, and almost none compare towns. The authors call for local studies with clear populations and periods.

title: Mobile money fraud and customer trust among students in Buea
snippet: A survey of 320 students in Buea found that 41% had received a fraudulent mobile money message in the past year. Trust in mobile money fell sharply after…
abstract: This article studies mobile money fraud and customer trust among university students in Buea. A survey of 320 students found that 41% had received a fraudulent message in the past year and 9% lost money. Students who lost money used mobile money less for six months. The study recommends awareness campaigns on campus and faster reversal of fraudulent transfers.

title: Factors affecting loan repayment among microfinance clients in Fako Division
snippet: Using data from 180 borrowers of three microfinance institutions in Fako, this project identifies business type, loan size and training as the main factors…
abstract: This project studied the factors affecting loan repayment among clients of three microfinance institutions in Fako Division. Data from 180 borrowers were analysed with logistic regression. Clients who received business training and borrowed smaller first loans repaid on time more often. Loans used for household needs were more likely to default.

title: Determinants of tax compliance among small and medium enterprises in Bafoussam
snippet: This paper studies why SMEs in Bafoussam comply or not with tax obligations. Complexity of procedures and perceived unfairness were the strongest predictors…
abstract: The paper studies the determinants of tax compliance among small and medium enterprises in Bafoussam. Using a survey of 260 SMEs, it finds that complex procedures, perceived unfairness and low trust in how taxes are used reduce compliance. Online declaration increased compliance among younger owners.

title: Influence of social media marketing on customer purchase decisions in Bamenda supermarkets
snippet: A study of 150 customers in three Bamenda supermarkets. Facebook and WhatsApp promotions influenced 62% of first visits, but price remained the main reason…
abstract: This project examined the influence of social media marketing on purchase decisions of supermarket customers in Bamenda. A questionnaire was answered by 150 customers. Facebook and WhatsApp promotions influenced 62% of first visits, while price and location drove repeat purchases. The study recommends combining online promotions with loyalty offers.

title: Service quality and customer satisfaction in commercial banks in Yaoundé
snippet: Using the SERVQUAL model with 300 bank customers in Yaoundé, the study finds that responsiveness and reliability explain most of the variation in satisfaction…
abstract: This study measures service quality and customer satisfaction in commercial banks in Yaoundé using the SERVQUAL model. Data from 300 customers show that responsiveness and reliability explain most differences in satisfaction. Long queues were the most common complaint.

title: Effect of motivation on employee performance in selected hotels in Limbe
snippet: This research assessed how pay, recognition and working conditions affect performance of 96 hotel employees in Limbe. Recognition had the strongest…
abstract: The research assessed the effect of motivation on the performance of employees in five hotels in Limbe. Data from 96 employees were collected by questionnaire and interviews with managers. Recognition and fair working hours had stronger effects than small pay rises. The study recommends regular recognition schemes.

title: 50 mobile money project topics for final year students (free PDF)
snippet: Here are 50 ready-made project topics on mobile money! Choose one, download chapter one to five and submit fast. WhatsApp us for the complete work…
abstract: A website selling complete projects. The topics are copied from old projects and the chapters are sold to many students. Submitting bought work is plagiarism: supervisors and juries recognise these projects, and they can lead to failure or cancellation of the degree.

title: Traders complain as mobile money charges rise in Douala markets
snippet: Market traders in Douala say new withdrawal charges are pushing customers back to cash. "I lose customers every day," said a trader at Marché Central…
abstract: A news report: traders in Douala markets say higher withdrawal charges push customers back to cash. News articles are useful to show that a problem is real and current (in your background), but they are not research evidence. Look for studies that measured the problem.

site: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences
title: Knowledge and use of insecticide-treated nets among pregnant women in Buea Health District
snippet: A cross-sectional study of 285 pregnant women attending antenatal care in Buea. 88% knew nets prevent malaria but only 57% slept under one the previous night…
abstract: This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge and use of insecticide-treated nets among 285 pregnant women attending antenatal care in Buea Health District. Most women knew that nets prevent malaria (88%), but only 57% slept under a net the previous night. Heat and net damage were the main reasons for not using them.
venue: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences

title: Factors influencing exclusive breastfeeding among mothers in Bamenda Regional Hospital
snippet: This study of 120 mothers with infants under 6 months found that returning to work and family pressure were the main barriers to exclusive breastfeeding…
abstract: This project studied the factors influencing exclusive breastfeeding among mothers of infants under six months at Bamenda Regional Hospital. Data from 120 mothers show that returning to work early and pressure from relatives to give water or porridge were the main barriers. Mothers counselled during antenatal visits breastfed exclusively more often.

site: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences
title: Awareness of hypertension among adults in rural communities of Meme Division
snippet: Blood pressure was measured in 410 adults in four villages of Meme. 31% had hypertension and two thirds of them did not know. Awareness was lowest among…
abstract: This study measured blood pressure and awareness of hypertension in 410 adults in four rural communities of Meme Division. 31% had hypertension, and two thirds of them did not know. Awareness was lowest among men and people over 60 who never visited a health centre.
venue: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences

title: Barriers to antenatal care attendance among pregnant women in Kumba Health District
snippet: Interviews with 24 women and a survey of 160 showed that distance, cost of tests and insecurity reduced antenatal care visits. Only 46% attended four visits…
abstract: This project examined barriers to antenatal care attendance among pregnant women in Kumba Health District, using a survey of 160 women and 24 interviews. Only 46% attended the recommended four visits. Distance, cost of laboratory tests and insecurity were the main barriers.

site: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences
title: Self-medication practices among university students in Douala
snippet: Of 390 students surveyed, 73% had taken medicine without prescription in the last six months, mostly painkillers and antibiotics bought from street vendors…
abstract: This survey of 390 university students in Douala studied self-medication practices. 73% had taken medicine without prescription in the past six months, mostly painkillers and antibiotics, often bought from street vendors. Cost of consultation and long waiting times were the main reasons.
venue: Mount Fako Journal of Health Sciences

title: Malaria – Open Encyclopedia
snippet: Malaria is a disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and spread by Anopheles mosquitoes. It remains one of the leading causes of illness in sub-Saharan Africa…
abstract: An encyclopedia overview of malaria: causes, symptoms, prevention and treatment. Good for understanding the subject, but not a source to cite in your project. Use the studies listed in its references instead.

title: Challenges of online learning in universities in Cameroon during and after COVID-19
snippet: A survey of 512 students and 48 lecturers in three universities. Poor internet, cost of data and lack of training for lecturers were the main challenges…
abstract: This article examines the challenges of online learning in three Cameroonian universities during and after COVID-19. Data from 512 students and 48 lecturers show that poor internet connection, the cost of data and lack of lecturer training were the main problems. Students in towns adapted better than those in rural areas.

title: Teacher motivation and students' academic performance in public secondary schools in Wouri Division
snippet: Data from 85 teachers and the GCE results of their schools show a positive link between teacher motivation and pass rates. Delayed salaries and large classes…
abstract: This project investigated the relationship between teacher motivation and students' academic performance in public secondary schools in Wouri Division. Questionnaires from 85 teachers were compared with school GCE pass rates. Schools with more motivated teachers had higher pass rates. Delayed salaries and very large classes lowered motivation.

title: Causes of absenteeism among primary school pupils in rural Menoua
snippet: Attendance registers and interviews with parents in 12 schools show that farm work during planting season and distance to school explain most absences…
abstract: The study explored causes of absenteeism among primary school pupils in 12 rural schools of Menoua. Attendance registers and interviews with parents show that farm work during planting season and long distances to school explain most absences.

title: Smartphone use and academic performance of university students in Bamenda
snippet: This study compared daily smartphone use and grade point averages of 230 students. Heavy social media use late at night was linked to lower GPA, while…
abstract: This project examined smartphone use and the academic performance of 230 university students in Bamenda. Heavy social media use late at night was linked to lower grade point averages, while students who used educational apps performed slightly better.

title: Cybersecurity awareness among small businesses using mobile banking in Douala
snippet: Of 140 small business owners, 64% reused the same PIN for several services and 38% had shared their PIN with an employee. Awareness training reduced…
abstract: This study measured cybersecurity awareness among 140 small business owners using mobile banking in Douala. 64% reused the same PIN across services and 38% had shared a PIN with an employee. A short awareness training reduced risky behaviour after three months.

title: Design and implementation of a web-based student information system for a secondary school in Buea
snippet: This project designed a web system for registration, fees and results at a secondary school in Buea. Testing with 12 staff reduced report card preparation…
abstract: This project designed and implemented a web-based student information system for registration, fees and results at a secondary school in Buea. User testing with 12 staff members showed that preparing report cards took two days instead of a week. The project includes the requirements, database design and test results.

title: Adoption of mobile agricultural information apps by farmers in the West Region
snippet: Using the Technology Acceptance Model, a survey of 200 farmers shows that perceived usefulness and local language support drive adoption of farming apps…
abstract: This study applied the Technology Acceptance Model to the adoption of mobile agricultural information apps by 200 farmers in the West Region. Perceived usefulness and support in local languages were the strongest drivers of adoption. Cost of data and low literacy were barriers.

title: Computer science project ideas that are not a management system?
snippet: "Everybody in my class is doing a management system. My supervisor wants something original. Any ideas?" – 32 replies
abstract: A forum thread where students share ideas. Replies suggest starting from a real problem in a real place (a clinic queue, a market, a council office). Good for ideas, but not a source to cite.

title: Effect of fertilizer use on cocoa yields among smallholder farmers in Meme Division
snippet: Yields of 160 smallholder cocoa farms were compared over two seasons. Farms using recommended fertilizer doses produced 38% more, but cost limited…
abstract: This study compared cocoa yields on 160 smallholder farms in Meme Division over two seasons. Farms using the recommended fertilizer doses produced 38% more cocoa. The high cost of fertilizer and late delivery limited use.

title: Post-harvest losses of maize among smallholder farmers in Ndop
snippet: Farmers in Ndop lost an estimated 22% of their maize after harvest, mostly to insects and moisture during storage. Hermetic bags reduced losses to…
abstract: This project estimated post-harvest losses of maize among 110 smallholder farmers in Ndop. Farmers lost about 22% of their maize after harvest, mostly to insects and moisture in storage. Farmers using hermetic storage bags lost less than 5%.

title: Farmers' perception of climate change and adaptation strategies in the North West Region (report)
snippet: This report summarises focus groups with 300 farmers in 15 villages. Most farmers noticed later rains and shorter seasons. Common responses were changing planting…
abstract: A report from a farmers' organisation summarising focus groups with 300 farmers in 15 villages of the North West Region. Most noticed later rains and shorter seasons. Common responses were changing planting dates and crop varieties. Reports like this are useful evidence, but check who wrote them and how the data were collected.

title: Determinants of youth participation in agriculture in Fako Division
snippet: A survey of 240 young people aged 18–35 found that access to land and credit, not lack of interest, were the main reasons young people avoided farming…
abstract: This study surveyed 240 young people aged 18 to 35 in Fako Division on their participation in agriculture. Access to land and to credit, not lack of interest, were the main reasons young people avoided farming. Youths with family land were three times more likely to farm.

title: Youth unemployment and the mismatch between university training and labour market needs in Cameroon
snippet: Using a tracer study of 600 graduates from four universities, the paper finds that 47% were unemployed two years after graduation, with large differences…
abstract: This paper uses a tracer study of 600 graduates from four universities to study youth unemployment. 47% were unemployed two years after graduation. Graduates with internships or practical training found work faster. The paper calls for closer links between universities and employers.

title: Contribution of remittances to household welfare in Dschang
snippet: Comparing 150 households that receive remittances with 150 that do not, the study finds higher spending on school fees and health among receiving households…
abstract: This project compared 150 households receiving remittances with 150 that do not in Dschang. Receiving households spent more on school fees and health care, but not on business investment. Most remittances arrived through mobile money.

title: Price of rice and oil up again: households in Buea cut meals
snippet: Families in Buea say they have reduced meals as food prices rise for the third time this year. Traders blame transport costs and import taxes…
abstract: A news article on rising food prices in Buea. It shows that the problem is current, which helps in your background, but it is not research evidence.

title: Customary land tenure and land disputes in the North West Region of Cameroon
snippet: An analysis of 74 court cases and interviews with traditional authorities shows that unregistered customary land is at the centre of most disputes…
abstract: This article analyses 74 court cases and interviews with traditional authorities on land disputes in the North West Region. Most disputes involve unregistered customary land and unclear boundaries. The author recommends simpler registration and recognition of customary mediation.

title: Legal protection of children against child labour in Cameroon: the case of plantation work in Fako
snippet: This dissertation examines how laws on child labour are applied on plantations in Fako. Interviews with labour inspectors show weak inspection and…
abstract: This dissertation examines the legal protection of children against child labour, using plantation work in Fako as a case study. It reviews national laws and international conventions and interviews labour inspectors. Laws are adequate on paper, but inspection is rare and penalties are seldom applied.

title: Access to justice for victims of domestic violence in Yaoundé
snippet: Interviews with 30 victims and 12 legal practitioners show that cost, fear of stigma and long procedures prevent most victims from going to court…
abstract: This qualitative study interviewed 30 victims of domestic violence and 12 legal practitioners in Yaoundé. Cost, fear of stigma and long procedures prevent most victims from going to court. Legal aid clinics helped the few who used them.

title: Household plastic waste management practices in Douala III Municipality
snippet: Observation and a survey of 300 households show that 58% burn or dump plastic waste because collection is irregular. Willingness to sort waste was high…
abstract: This study surveyed 300 households in Douala III Municipality on plastic waste management. 58% burn or dump plastic waste because collection is irregular. Most households said they would sort waste if collection were reliable.

title: Causes and effects of urban flooding in Limbe, 2010–2021
snippet: Using rainfall data, satellite images and interviews with 90 residents, this study links flooding to blocked drains and building in waterways…
abstract: This project studied the causes and effects of urban flooding in Limbe between 2010 and 2021, using rainfall data, satellite images and interviews with 90 residents. Flooding was linked to blocked drains and construction in waterways more than to rainfall alone.

title: Forest cover loss around Kribi: drivers and community responses (policy report)
snippet: Satellite data show a 12% loss of forest cover around Kribi between 2014 and 2023, mainly due to farming, wood fuel and new infrastructure…
abstract: A policy report using satellite data and community meetings around Kribi. Forest cover fell by 12% between 2014 and 2023, mainly due to farming, wood fuel and new infrastructure. Reports from institutes can be cited, but note that they are not peer reviewed.

title: Research Methods for Undergraduate Projects (3rd ed.)
snippet: A step-by-step guide to choosing a topic, writing objectives, designing a questionnaire, sampling and analysing data for final year projects…
abstract: A textbook for undergraduate projects: topic selection, objectives, research design, sampling, questionnaires and simple analysis. Textbooks are good sources for your methodology chapter.
